title: Creole identity today and African dress
summary: Tex closes on writers like Lyle Saxon, who calls himself Creole today, and changing black fashion.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers

blocks.x: I agree with you 100% so all in all

like I'm saying to each his own but this Creole thing we will always have people like Lyle Saxon and all these other writers of note who will write about them and talk about them but like I said it all depends on who they're talking about what era of time what went on back in the 1840s 1830s and so forth before you get into the 1900s but today we got a lot of people who call themselves Creole we got an element of blacks out in California who call themselves Creoles and I think De Picayune did a story on it some time back but then again you've got people today who just feel to believe that the high Yala people there's no place for them that everybody got to be real dark you got element of people today want to wear dashikis and they talk about wearing these big bushes but then again when I think about I'm looking at Mandela Mandela coming over dressed like me and I have a relative in Chicago like my sister and them who just came out of Africa and my brother-in-law they say blacks are not dressing like that in South Africa with all them loud colors they're following the trend like they want to be like Mr. Mandela they want to be some Johnston Murphy shoes on they wanted some live on $350 suits or they want some cultured $975 dollars for the suits like that
